questions.text: What is the theory that Earth's outer shell is broken into moving plates called?
At which type of plate boundary do volcanoes MOST commonly form?
The Philippine Fault System is an example of which plate boundary type?
How were the Philippine islands primarily formed?
options: Through volcanic arcs, collisions, and tectonic uplift over millions of years
They were carried to their current location by ocean currents
They are fragments of the Moon that broke off long ago
They were always a single big island that later fragmented
questions.correct: Through volcanic arcs, collisions, and tectonic uplift over millions of years

questions.text: What is the Pacific Ring of Fire?
options: A horseshoe-shaped zone around the Pacific where most volcanoes and earthquakes occur
A ring of fire in Hawaii
questions.correct: A horseshoe-shaped zone around the Pacific where most volcanoes and earthquakes occur

questions.text: Why are marine fossils found on Philippine mountains?
options: The ocean once covered the area, and tectonic uplift raised the land above sea level
Fish used to live on dry land millions of years ago
Ancient people carried the fossils up the mountains
They fell from the sky during meteor showers long ago
questions.correct: The ocean once covered the area, and tectonic uplift raised the land above sea level

_tag.rationale: Philippine geology landform analysis; distractors balanced (Phase 6)

questions.text: Which tectonic plate subducts beneath Luzon and the Visayas, creating volcanoes and trenches?
What geological feature is east of Mindanao and reaches depths of over 10,000 meters?
Which of the following landforms is a karst landscape with an underground river?
Which of the following describes the Chocolate Hills of Bohol?
options: Rounded hills formed by weathering of limestone
Ancient volcanic craters filled with rainwater
Wind-blown sand dunes from a prehistoric desert
Raised coral reefs from a shallow ancient sea
questions.correct: Rounded hills formed by weathering of limestone

questions.text: How many climate types does PAGASA classify in the Philippines?
Which monsoon wind brings cool, dry weather from November to February?
About how many tropical cyclones enter Philippine waters each year?
Which region of the Philippines typically has Type II climate (no dry season, rainfall throughout the year)?
What is the Coral Triangle?
options: A marine region including the Philippines with 2,500+ fish species and 500+ coral species
A political alliance of three countries
questions.correct: A marine region including the Philippines with 2,500+ fish species and 500+ coral species

questions.text: About what percentage of Philippine plants are endemic (found only in the Philippines)?
Which iconic Philippine species is one of the largest eagles in the world and is critically endangered?
Which small buffalo species is found ONLY in Mindoro?
Which of the following is the MOST serious threat to Philippine biodiversity?
options: Habitat loss from deforestation, mining, and land conversion
Too many protected areas being set aside by government
Overpopulation of endemic species in the wild
Excessive rainfall and flooding during typhoon season
questions.correct: Habitat loss from deforestation, mining, and land conversion

questions.text: The Philippines is one of 17 megadiverse countries. What does this mean?
options: It contains a very high number of species, many of which are endemic
It has the largest total land area in the world
It has the highest human population density
It has the most active volcanoes in the world
questions.correct: It contains a very high number of species, many of which are endemic
